purpose: Show that ordinal mismatch transitions do not collapse into equal numeric spacing, units, or metric distance.

counterexample_case.label: Equal ordinal step count without equal metric meaning
counterexample_case.setup: Trace T1 moves LOW_MISMATCH to MODERATE_MISMATCH because A changes under a fixed declared <S>. Trace T2 moves MODERATE_MISMATCH to HIGH_MISMATCH because r_a changes after reference rebinding.
counterexample_case.result: Both traces count as one ordinal step, but they do not determine the same magnitude, interval, or numeric distance.

misreadings_blocked: A local step is not a unit interval.
One ordinal transition is not a scalar magnitude.
A jump transition is not a Euclidean leap.
ADMISSIBILITY_BREAK is not a metric maximum.
No class here implies a numeric norm.
forbidden_inference: Ordinal class movement does not imply numeric distance.
Ordinal class movement does not imply physical measurement.
Ordinal class movement does not imply topology.
Ordinal class movement does not imply role symmetry.
Ordinal class movement does not modify RT_core.

non_claims: Does not prove impossibility of all metrics.
Does not prove impossibility of all metrics.
